To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we can use linked lexical knowledge base to improve lexicon and training data coverage in SRL, 2) we can use knowledge base links to generate predicate and role labels for unlabeled data, and 3) the resulting training data can be used to improve the performance of SRL systems.

(i) We developed methods to generate large amounts of training data for semantic role labeling using linked lexical knowledge bases, which can be used to improve the performance of supervised SRL methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following research questions: How can we improve lexicon coverage for SRL using linked lexical knowledge bases?
the following two research questions: (1) Can we improve lexicon coverage by linking lexical knowledge bases?
the following research questions: 1) How can knowledge-based methods be used for lexicon coverage improvement?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed a novel approach to knowledge-based SRL that can be applied to any language for which a lexical knowledge base is available.
knowledge-based methods can be used to improve lexicon and training data coverage in a domain-adaptive way, but they have to be combined with other methods to reach state-of-the-art performance.
the knowledge-based methods for domain-adaptive semantic role labeling proposed and developed in this thesis are a valuable addition to the current state-of-the-art.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a method for knowledge-based supervision of semantic role labeling, which allows us to extend the lexica of semantic role labeling systems and to automatically generate training data for semantic role labeling.

we were able to show that knowledge-based methods are a promising alternative to corpus-based methods for the domain-adaptation and lexicon coverage problem for Semantic Role Labeling in German and Spanish.
we have shown that knowledge-based supervision is a feasible and promising approach to address the lexicon and training data coverage issues for SRL in a domain-agnostic and cross-lingual way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of knowledge-based methods for lexicon coverage and automatic training data generation can significantly improve the performance of SRL systems.
linked lexical resources can be used to improve the coverage of SRL in a knowledge-based way and that this is particularly useful for languages with only small amounts of training data available.
knowledge-based methods for lexicon coverage and domain adaptation can improve the coverage of SRL systems.
